silhouette.reason: panel-1: Clearly an armoured orc warrior bust: spiked dome pauldrons, topknot, swept ears, lower tusks and a hulking trapezius read in every black view. Side view is a lumpy pear where the skull, traps and pauldron merge, and the beard's blocky rectangle flattens the jaw line in front. | panel-2: Strong, readable outline: spiked pauldrons, topknot, pointed ears, tusks and a wide neckless mass say armoured orc in every view. The front outline is a clear cross shape. Weak points: the topknot is a thick bent hose rather than hair, the tusks do not break the outline in front view, and the side view is a round ball with the face barely projecting. | panel-3: Front silhouette is instantly an orc warlord: wide spiked pauldrons, topknot, pointed ears, massive trapezius. The side view weakens it: head and torso merge into one pear/egg blob with no jaw-to-neck break, and the tusks barely break the outline.
fixes: Separate the jaw from the traps in side view with a deeper under-jaw shadow line and a forward-thrust lower jaw
Taper the beard to a point or braids so it breaks the rectangular front block
Make the ears larger and angled outward so they clear the skull outline
Rebuild the topknot as a bound tail of strands with a flared end
Lengthen and splay the tusks so they clear the cheeks in front view
Push the brow and jaw forward in profile so the face projects past the chest
Push the lower jaw forward and down so an underbite and jaw corner separate head from trapezius in side view
Lengthen the tusks so they clear the upper lip and read in silhouette
Flatten the back of the torso and add a shoulder-blade plane so the side reads as a body, not an egg

proportions.reason: panel-1: Good orc mass: no visible neck, huge traps, heavy brow. But the cranium is a tall narrow egg rising above a smallish face, the nose is a soft blob, the eyes sit high and tiny under the brow, and the lower jaw (which carries the tusks) is not wide or protruding enough; tusks look stuck on rather than rooted in an underbite. Pauldrons are large relative to the shoulder they sit on. | panel-2: Heavy jaw, wide skull and bull neck fit an orc, and the pauldrons are a believable size. Errors: the eyes are tiny glowing dots set high and close with no visible eyeball or lids, the nose is a soft lump, the ear is a thin vertical blade with no concha, the skull is a smooth egg merging into a spherical torso with no trapezius, clavicle or pectoral forms, and the lower teeth sit as a row of pegs on the lip. The pauldrons float beside the body without straps to the torso. | panel-3: Heavy brow, wide nose and huge trapezius are on-model for an orc, but the cranium is a smooth tall dome that is too small at the back, the ears are tiny and placed high above the eye line, eyes are tiny glowing slits sunk without lids, and the tusks root in the lip corners rather than the lower jaw.
fixes: Lower and widen the cranium; push the brow ridge forward as a heavy shelf
Widen and protrude the mandible so tusks emerge from a clear underbite
Define the nose with a broad flattened bridge and flared nostrils
Scale the pauldrons down ~10% or widen the deltoids under them
Model real eyeballs in deep orbits under the brow; keep the glow as emissive iris only
Sculpt nostrils and a broad nose with alar wings
Give the ears thickness, a concha and a notched rim
Add trapezius, clavicles and pectoral planes to the torso mass
Seat the teeth in a lower gum line; attach pauldrons with visible straps and buckles to the harness
Widen the jaw and cheekbones and lower the cranium height for a brutish wide-low skull
Move ears down to brow-to-nose height and enlarge them
Seat the tusks in a protruding lower jaw with visible gums
Give the eyes modelled lids under the brow shelf instead of emissive dots

materials.reason: panel-1: Best material separation of the set: steel pauldrons reflect with a proper highlight and rust bleeding at rivets, bone spikes and tusks read as ivory, leather belt is brown and matte, skin has a mottled green with some sheen. Weak spots: the fur cape is smooth clay with no hair, the beard is dense but flat, and the topknot hair is a smooth rubbery tube. | panel-2: Best material read of the set: steel pauldrons are metallic with highlights and rust patches, bone spikes and tusks are matte ivory, leather strap is brown with a metal buckle, skin is mottled green. Skin is uniformly rough with a cloth-like grain, the topknot and the fur mantle read as brown clay, and the rust is orange decals rather than pitted metal. | panel-3: Steel pauldrons read as metal with specular, rivets and rust bleed; bone spikes and tusks separate as ivory; the leather belt and fur mantle read by hue. Skin is a uniform olive with odd pale vertical streaks on the face; the beard is a dark noisy curtain; the topknot looks like brown plastic.
fixes: Give the cape fur cards or a fur shell with a ragged edge instead of a smooth draped slab
Make the topknot a braided strand set with roughness variation, not a smooth tube
Add skin roughness variation and subtle warmer tint at lips, ears and knuckles of the face
Add specular variation to skin and a pore normal in place of the woven grain
Give the topknot and fur mantle strand cards or a fur normal with anisotropy
Raise rust roughness and add height so it pits the steel; add edge wear highlights on plate rims
Yellow the tusk roots and add fine cracks
Replace the pale face streaks with deliberate war paint or scars with edges
Give the topknot strand clumping and a leather wrap instead of a smooth tube
Add skin colour zoning (darker brow and knuckles of the face, warmer lips and ears)
Raise roughness on the fur mantle and add tip highlights

detail.reason: panel-1: Pauldrons have rivets, layered lames, banding and spikes; belt has a buckle; a bone-bead necklace and warpaint streak add interest. The face is softer: few wrinkles, little scarring relief, teeth are small pegs, and ears lack inner structure. The fur cape and back are underdeveloped. | panel-2: Rivets on the plates, layered lames, a buckle, a bone-bead necklace, strand beard, brow hairs and facial scars give real density, and the detail map is busy across the armour. Close up the back is weak: the topknot is a smooth tube with fused finger-like strands, the fur mantle is a draped sheet with drip-shaped ends, the skin is featureless on skull and back, and the beard is straight vertical cards with a hard top edge on the cheeks. | panel-3: Best detail of the set: riveted layered pauldrons, bone-bead necklace, buckle, belt, teeth row, brow wrinkles. Still missing scars, skin pores, ear structure, stitching on the leather and fur strand definition.
fixes: Sculpt brow furrows, nose-bridge creases and a raised scar across the face
Model gums and a fuller lower tooth row with the tusks set in sockets
Add straps and buckles holding the pauldrons to the torso
Detail the inner ear and add a ring or notch
Add wrinkles at the brow, nose and neck folds and veins on the skull
Replace the mantle with layered fur tufts and a stitched leather edge
Blend the beard into the cheeks with shorter cards and stubble; vary card direction
Add dents, scratches and a rolled edge to the pauldron plates
Add scars across brow and cheek, nicks in the ears and ear rings
Stitch the belt and add a strap holding each pauldron
Sculpt fur clumps on the mantle edge

Skin is too clean and evenly coloured, the steel is still mostly mirror-polished, and there are no dents or chipped edges on the armour. | panel-2: Rust on the pauldrons, pale scars across the cheek and brow, stained teeth and a ragged mantle tell some history. fixes: Add dents and edge chipping to pauldron rims and dull the steel in recesses
Put battle scars, dirt and sweat sheen on the face and shoulders
Stain and fray the belt edges and dirty the bone beads
Drive rust from rivets, plate overlaps and lower edges with streaks running down
Add sword nicks and dents to one pauldron and a broken spike tip
Darken and crack the leather strap at the buckle holes
Add grime in skin folds and a chipped tusk
Dent and scratch the pauldrons, especially the leading edges
Chip a tusk and stain the tusk bases
Add dirt and dried blood in skin folds and under the beard

Keep eye glow the same screen size as LOD0
Keep ear length and tusk angle at LOD2
Keep the leather strap and rust tint as vertex colour at LOD2
Replace LOD2 beard blob with a tapered, jagged beard card shape matching LOD0 colour
Keep the brow shelf and eye sockets as geometry so eyes sit under the brow
Keep a simplified mantle silhouette at LOD2
